usage: papers init [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                   [--porcelain] [--name-template NAME_TEMPLATE]
                   [--name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM]
                   [--name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP]
                   [--name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                   [--name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                   [--name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH]
                   [--name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP]
                   [--name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                   [--name-unknown-strict | --no-name-unknown-strict]
                   [--key-template KEY_TEMPLATE]
                   [--key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM]
                   [--key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP]
                   [--key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                   [--key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                   [--key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH]
                   [--key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP]
                   [--key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                   [--key-unknown-strict | --no-key-unknown-strict]
                   [--bibtex BIBTEX] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--pool PATH]
                   [--shallow] [--global] [--paths {relative,absolute}]
                   [--editor EDITOR]
                   [DIR]

create a library in the current directory, or in DIR (created if missing): a
self-contained library (its own entries and files, no pool), or with --pool
PATH a shallow library, which takes its entries from the library PATH and
links to its files. It asks no questions: every setting has a default (from
the global configuration, or built in), the options below override them, and
later changes go through `papers config`.

positional arguments:
  DIR                   directory of the library (default: the current
                        directory); like DIR, the paths of --bibtex,
                        --filesdir and --pool are relative to the current
                        directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex file (default: papers.bib, or the first .bib
                        file of the directory)
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: files, or an existing pdfs/,
                        papers/... folder)
  --pool PATH           a shallow library that uses the library PATH as pool
                        (PATH must be a library without pool; a relative PATH
                        is stored relative to the library): `papers add` looks
                        in PATH first and adds the new entries and their files
                        to it, and the library links to the files of PATH.
                        Default: no pool, a self-contained library
  --shallow             same as --pool with the default library (`papers
                        config --global default`)
  --global              also register the library as the default library (used
                        outside of any library, and by --shallow); DIR is
                        required (`papers init . --global` for the current
                        directory)
  --paths {relative,absolute}
                        file links in the bibtex relative to the bibtex
                        directory, or absolute (default: absolute)
  --editor EDITOR       command to open a text editor; it must wait until the
                        editor is closed, e.g. vim or "subl -w"

filename format:
  --name-template NAME_TEMPLATE
                        python template for renaming files (default:
                        {title}-{year})
  --name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the filename (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 5)
  --name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the filename (default: +)
  --name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the filename
                        (default: 100)
  --name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the filename (default: 1)
  --name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the filename (the last
                        words are dropped until it fits; a longer first word
                        is cut) (default: 100)
  --name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the filename (default:
                        -)
  --name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the filename of an entry without author,
                        year or title (default: unknown_{doi_or_id})
  --name-unknown-strict, --no-name-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: True)

bibtex key format:
  --key-template KEY_TEMPLATE
                        python template for generating keys (default: {year}).
                        The template applies to entries generated from a PDF
                        or a DOI; entries added from a bibtex file keep their
                        original key unless -u/--update-key is passed.
  --key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the key (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the key (default: _)
  --key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the key (default:
                        100)
  --key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the key (default: 1)
  --key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the key (the last words
                        are dropped until it fits; a longer first word is cut)
                        (default: 20)
  --key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the key (default: - )
  --key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the key of an entry without author, year
                        or title (default: {doi_})
  --key-unknown-strict, --no-key-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)

usage: papers add [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                  [--porcelain] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--bibtex BIBTEX]
                  [--dry-run] [--name-template NAME_TEMPLATE]
                  [--name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM]
                  [--name-author-sep NAME_AUTHOR_SEP]
                  [--name-title-word-num NAME_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                  [--name-title-word-size NAME_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                  [--name-title-length NAME_TITLE_LENGTH]
                  [--name-title-sep NAME_TITLE_SEP]
                  [--name-unknown-template NAME_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                  [--name-unknown-strict | --no-name-unknown-strict]
                  [--key-template KEY_TEMPLATE]
                  [--key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM]
                  [--key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP]
                  [--key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM]
                  [--key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE]
                  [--key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH]
                  [--key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP]
                  [--key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE]
                  [--key-unknown-strict | --no-key-unknown-strict]
                  [--format {bibtex,ris,csl-json,bibjson}]
                  [--on-duplicate {ask,keep,update,skip,error}]
                  [--no-check-duplicate] [--no-pool] [--pool PATH] [-u] [-R]
                  [--ignore-errors] [--doi DOI] [--key KEY] [--type TYPE]
                  [--title TITLE] [--author AUTHOR] [-a NAME [NAME ...]]
                  [--journal JOURNAL] [--year YEAR]
                  [--metadata FIELD=VALUE [FIELD=VALUE ...]] [--no-query-doi]
                  [--no-query-fulltext] [--scholar] [--attach FILE [FILE ...]]
                  [--move] [-r] [-c] [--link] [-e] [-o]
                  [file ...]

add PDF(s), bibtex(s), RIS (.ris) or CSL-JSON (.json) file(s) to library. In a
shallow library, the files go to the files directory of the pool (files mode
move or copy; with link, they stay where they are), and the entries to the
pool too. Adding a bibtex file (`papers add other.bib`) copies its entries
once, with no memory of where they came from; `papers pull` instead keeps the
entries linked to the pool, and later pulls bring its corrections.

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --format {bibtex,ris,csl-json,bibjson}
                        the format of the added files that are not PDFs
                        (default: from the extension: .ris is RIS, .json is
                        CSL-JSON, .bib.json is BibJSON, other files are
                        bibtex). RIS needs the rispy package.

  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex database (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-

  --dry-run             no PDF renaming/copying, no bibtex writing on disk
                        (for testing)

duplicate check:
  An added entry is the same paper as a library entry when they have the
  same DOI, arXiv id, ISBN (two books), or else the same authors and title.
  The library entry keeps its key; fields only in the added entry are added
  and the file links are merged. An entry that brings nothing new is not
  asked about.

  --on-duplicate {ask,keep,update,skip,error}
                        what to do when the added entry is in the library,
                        with conflicting values or fields to add: ask
                        (dialogue; the default in a terminal), keep (merge,
                        conflicts keep the library's value: the library
                        receives the entry), update (merge, conflicts take the
                        value of the added entry), skip (leave the library
                        entry untouched, do not add), error (stop before
                        saving; the default without a terminal)
  --no-check-duplicate  disable duplicate check (faster, create duplicates)
  --no-pool             do not look in the pool first (by default, a PDF, DOI
                        or bibtex entry that is the same paper as a pool entry
                        is taken from the pool, with its files, without
                        fetching)
  --pool PATH           look in the library PATH first, instead of the pool
                        (PATH must be a library without pool): a paper that
                        PATH has is taken from it, with its files (copied as
                        the files mode says; in a shallow library, into the
                        files directory of its pool), and later `papers pull
                        --pool PATH` brings its corrections. Nothing is added
                        to PATH. Not the same as `papers -C PATH add`, which
                        adds to the library PATH.
  -u, --update-key      regenerate the key of the entries new to the library
                        from the key template (see "bibtex key format"
                        options). A duplicate always keeps the key of the
                        library.

directory scan:
  -R, --recursive       accept directory as argument, for recursive scan of
                        .pdf and .bib files; files named <name>--<label>.<ext>
                        next to <name>.pdf are added as attachments of its
                        entry
  --ignore-errors       ignore errors when adding multiple files

metadata:
  The fields given here replace those found in the PDF, fetched from the
  DOI, or read from the added bibtex (one entry only). They do not change an
  entry already in the library (same DOI): use `papers edit`.

  --doi DOI             provide DOI -- skip parsing PDF
  --key KEY             the key of the entry (instead of a key made from the
                        key template); alone, the entry of that key is taken
                        from the pool
  --type TYPE           entry type (article, book...)
  --title TITLE         the title
  --author AUTHOR       the authors, e.g. "Smith, John and Doe, Jane"
  -a NAME [NAME ...]    same as --author (the values after the name are files
                        to add, as the FILE arguments). In papers v2, -a
                        FILE... attached files: when every value of -a is an
                        existing file (or a URL), they are attached as with
                        --attach, with a warning (until v4)
  --journal JOURNAL     the journal
  --year YEAR           the year
  --metadata FIELD=VALUE [FIELD=VALUE ...]
                        any fields
  --no-query-doi        do not attempt to parse and query doi
  --no-query-fulltext   do not attempt to query fulltext in case doi query
                        fails
  --scholar             use google scholar instead of crossref

files:
  What happens to the added PDF, the files of an added bibtex, and the
  attached files, is the `files` setting of the library (found: move): move:
  place them in the files directory, under a name made from the name
  template, and remove the original; copy: place them there, and keep the
  original (a hard link when possible, otherwise a copy); link: leave them
  where they are, the entry links to them there. A file that belongs to
  another library (inside its files directory) is never moved: it is copied
  instead. In a library that is shallow, the file links are those of the
  pool entry: move and copy place the files in the files directory of the
  pool, link leaves them where they are and the pool entry links to them
  there too.

  --attach FILE [FILE ...]
                        attach these files to the entry (e.g. supplementary
                        material)
  --move                files mode move, whatever the setting
  -r, --rename          same as --move
  -c, --copy            files mode copy, whatever the setting
  --link                files mode link, whatever the setting

actions:
  -e, --edit            edit entry
  -o, --open            open files

usage: papers rm [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                 [--porcelain] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--bibtex BIBTEX]
                 [--dry-run] [--delete-files] [--keep-files] [-y]
                 KEY [KEY ...]

remove entries. Their files that no other entry links to may be deleted too:
in a terminal, papers asks for those in the files directory; without a
terminal, they are kept. Files outside the files directory are only deleted
with --delete-files. In a shallow library, the files of the pool are kept:
`papers file rm FILE` deletes them.

positional arguments:
  KEY                   KEY: key, DOI, arXiv id or ISBN (a former key in the
                        ids field works too); - reads them from the standard
                        input, one per line

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --delete-files        also delete the files of the entries that no other
                        entry links to, without asking (also those outside the
                        files directory); an error in a shallow library
  --keep-files          keep the files, without asking
  -y, --yes             do not ask before deleting more files than the history
                        keeps (the history-size setting)

config:
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-
                        lib/pdfs)
  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex database (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-
                        lib/library.bib)
  --dry-run             no PDF renaming/copying, no bibtex writing on disk
                        (for testing)

usage: papers config [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                     [--porcelain] [--unset KEY] [--prune] [--global] [-y]
                     [--dry-run]
                     [KEY] [VALUE ...]

get or set the settings of the library (git style): without KEY, list the
settings and where each comes from (library, global or default); with KEY,
print its value; with KEY VALUE..., set it in the library configuration

positional arguments:
  KEY
  VALUE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --unset KEY           remove the setting: the global or default value
                        applies again (pool: none)
  --prune               remove from the library configuration file the
                        settings equal to their global or default value (they
                        follow it from then on); a setting given explicitly
                        (`papers init`, `papers config NAME VALUE`) is kept in
                        the file, even with the default value
  --global              the global configuration, per user
                        (/private/tmp/papers-help-home/Library/Application
                        Support/papers/config.json), instead of the library's:
                        the default library, and the default settings of the
                        libraries
  -y, --yes             do not ask before copying or deleting the files (pool)
  --dry-run             do not save (pool: only show what would be done)

settings: bibtex, filesdir, pool, paths, files, auto-push, editor, checksums,
history-dir, history-size, history-separate, keep-deleted-files,
name.template, name.author-num, name.author-sep, name.title-word-num,
name.title-word-size, name.title-length, name.title-sep, name.unknown-
template, name.unknown-strict, key.template, key.author-num, key.author-sep,
key.title-word-num, key.title-word-size, key.title-length, key.title-sep,
key.unknown-template, key.unknown-strict; with --global, also default (the
default library: PATH or none). pool PATH (a library without pool, not the
library itself) makes the library shallow: it links to the pool's copies of
its PDFs, and its own copies are deleted; each PDF must be in the pool entry
already, otherwise nothing changes and papers names the entries to push first
(`papers push --pool PATH KEY...`). pool none makes a shallow library self-
contained: the pool files that it links to are copied into its files
directory. papers lists what it will do and asks to continue.

usage: papers file attach [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                          [--porcelain] [--filesdir FILESDIR]
                          [--bibtex BIBTEX] [--dry-run]
                          [--name-template NAME_TEMPLATE]
                          [--name-author-num NAME_AUTHOR_NUM]

                          [--name-unknown-strict | --no-name-unknown-strict]
                          [--move] [--copy] [--link]
                          KEY FILE [FILE ...]

attach files to an existing entry. What happens to the files is the files
setting (found: move), as for `papers add`; the files the entry had are left
as they are.

positional arguments:
  KEY                   key, DOI, arXiv id or ISBN of the entry
  FILE                  files or URLs

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}

usage: papers check [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                    [--porcelain] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--bibtex BIBTEX]
                    [--dry-run] [--key-template KEY_TEMPLATE]
                    [--key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM]
                    [--key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP]

                    [-k KEYS [KEYS ...]] [-y] [--fix-key] [--key-ascii]
                    [--auto-key] [--fix-doi] [--fetch] [--fetch-all]
                    [--format-name] [--encoding {latex,unicode}]
                    [--duplicates] [--on-duplicate {ask,keep,skip,error}]
                    [KEY ...]

check and fix entries

positional arguments:
  KEY                   check these entries only (default: all): KEY: key,
                        DOI, arXiv id or ISBN (a former key in the ids field
                        works too); - reads them from the standard input, one
                        per line

                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed

                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  -k, --keys KEYS [KEYS ...]
                        apply check on this key subset (same as the KEY
                        arguments)
  -y, --yes             do not ask: apply the changes of the fixes and fetches
                        (and --on-duplicate skip by default)

  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-

bibtex key format:
  --key-template KEY_TEMPLATE
                        python template for generating keys (default: {year}).
                        The template applies to entries generated from a PDF
                        or a DOI; entries added from a bibtex file keep their
                        original key unless -u/--update-key is passed.
  --key-author-num KEY_AUTHOR_NUM
                        number of authors in the key (not for {authorX})
                        (default: 2)
  --key-author-sep KEY_AUTHOR_SEP
                        separator of the authors in the key (default: _)
  --key-title-word-num KEY_TITLE_WORD_NUM
                        maximum number of title words in the key (default:
                        100)
  --key-title-word-size KEY_TITLE_WORD_SIZE
                        minimum length of a title word: shorter words are left
                        out of the key (default: 1)
  --key-title-length KEY_TITLE_LENGTH
                        maximum length of the title in the key (the last words
                        are dropped until it fits; a longer first word is cut)
                        (default: 20)
  --key-title-sep KEY_TITLE_SEP
                        separator of the title words in the key (default: - )
  --key-unknown-template KEY_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE
                        template of the key of an entry without author, year
                        or title (default: {doi_})
  --key-unknown-strict, --no-key-unknown-strict
                        the unknown template applies when the author, the year
                        or the title is missing; with this option, only when
                        all three are missing (default: False)

entry key:
  --fix-key             fix key based on author name and date (in case missing
                        or digit)
  --key-ascii           replace keys unicode character with ascii
  --auto-key            new, auto-generated key for all entries

crossref fetch and fix:
  --fix-doi             fix doi for some common issues (e.g. DOI: inside doi,
                        .received at the end
  --fetch               fetch metadata from doi and update entry
  --fetch-all           --fetch, and for entries without DOI, a crossref
                        search by title and authors. The best result is taken
                        only if its title is the same or nearly the same
                        (after normalization) and it has an author family name
                        in common with the entry; otherwise the entry is left
                        unchanged and a warning is printed. The fetched fields
                        replace or add to those of the entry; the key and the
                        files are kept. Asks before each change unless -y.

names:
  --format-name         author name as family, given, without brackets
  --encoding {latex,unicode}
                        bibtex field encoding

duplicates:
  --duplicates          merge the entries that are the same paper (same DOI,
                        arXiv id, ISBN of two books, or else same authors and
                        title). The entry with most fields is entry 1, the
                        target: it keeps its key, and the keys of the others
                        go to its ids field.
  --on-duplicate {ask,keep,skip,error}
                        what to do with each group: ask (dialogue; the default
                        in a terminal), keep (merge, conflicts keep the value
                        of entry 1), skip (leave the group), error (exit with
                        status 1 if there is any group; the default without a
                        terminal, and skip with -y/--yes)

usage: papers list [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                   [--porcelain] [--filesdir FILESDIR] [--bibtex BIBTEX]
                   [--dry-run] [--strict | --fuzzy]
                   [--fuzzy-ratio FUZZY_RATIO] [--invert] [--any]
                   [-a AUTHOR [AUTHOR ...]]
                   [--first-author FIRST_AUTHOR [FIRST_AUTHOR ...]]
                   [-y YEAR [YEAR ...]] [-t TITLE [TITLE ...]]
                   [--abstract ABSTRACT [ABSTRACT ...]] [-k KEY [KEY ...]]
                   [--doi DOI [DOI ...]] [--keywords KEYWORDS [KEYWORDS ...]]
                   [--by {key,doi,title}] [--duplicates] [--has-file]
                   [--no-file] [--broken-file] [--review-required]
                   [--format {line,bibtex,ris,csl-json,bibjson,key} |
                   --plain | -l | -K | --field FIELD [FIELD ...]] [--no-key]
                   [--delete] [--delete-files] [--keep-files] [-e]
                   [--add-keywords ADD_KEYWORDS [ADD_KEYWORDS ...]] [--rename]
                   [--keep-source] [-o] [--attach FILE [FILE ...]]
                   [--rm-tag TAG [TAG ...]] [--detach [FILE ...]]
                   [--detach-broken] [--fix-files [DIR ...]] [--move] [--push]
                   [--pull] [--sync] [--pool PATH]
                   [--on-duplicate {ask,keep,update,skip,error}]
                   [--export DIR] [--export-files {copy,link,none}]
                   [--export-format FORMAT]
                   [fullsearch ...]

list (a subset of) entries in the existing bib file

positional arguments:
  fullsearch            Search field. Usually no quotes required. See keywords
                        to search specific fields. All words must find a
                        match, unless --any is passed.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error (except the listing
                        of papers list, which stays on the standard output)
  --strict              exact matching - instead of substring
  --fuzzy               fuzzy matching - instead of substring
  --fuzzy-ratio FUZZY_RATIO
                        threshold for fuzzy matching of title, author,
                        abstract (default: 50), and of authors and title with
                        --duplicates --fuzzy (default: 80)
  --invert              list the entries that the same command without
                        --invert does not list
  --any                 when several keywords: any of them

config:
  --filesdir FILESDIR   files directory (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-
                        lib/pdfs)
  --bibtex BIBTEX       bibtex database (default: /private/tmp/papers-help-
                        lib/library.bib)
  --dry-run             no PDF renaming/copying, no bibtex writing on disk
                        (for testing)

search:
  -a, --author AUTHOR [AUTHOR ...]
                        any of the authors
  --first-author FIRST_AUTHOR [FIRST_AUTHOR ...]
                        family name of the first author
  -y, --year YEAR [YEAR ...]
                        year
  -t, --title TITLE [TITLE ...]
                        title
  --abstract ABSTRACT [ABSTRACT ...]
                        abstract
  -k, --key, --id KEY [KEY ...]
                        entry key
  --doi DOI [DOI ...]   DOI
  --keywords, --tag KEYWORDS [KEYWORDS ...]
                        keywords (tags): whole tags, case-insensitive, with *
                        patterns (--tag 'ice*'); a tag also finds the tags
                        under it (--tag climate: climate/amoc)

check:
  --by {key,doi,title}  with --duplicates (implied): the entries that share
                        this field instead (the same key, DOI, or title
                        ignoring case and punctuation), whether or not they
                        are the same paper
  --duplicates          entries that are the same paper, as `papers check
                        --duplicates` finds them, and the entries it would ask
                        about; with --fuzzy, also the entries with similar
                        authors and title (see --fuzzy-ratio)
  --has-file            entries with at least one file
  --no-file             entries without file
  --broken-file         entries with a file link to a missing file
  --review-required     suspicious entry (invalid dois, missing field etc.)

formatting:
  --format {line,bibtex,ris,csl-json,bibjson,key}
                        line: one line per entry (the default); bibtex, ris,
                        csl-json, bibjson: the entries in that format (file
                        links as absolute paths; RIS needs the rispy package);
                        key: the keys only, one per line (to pipe into the
                        commands that take -, e.g. `papers file rename -`)
  --plain               same as --format bibtex
  -l, -1, --one-liner   same as --format line
  -K, --key-only        same as --format key
  --field FIELD [FIELD ...]
                        print these fields only (after the key)
  --no-key              do not print the keys

action on listed results:
  run a command on the listed entries, in the same process (questions and
  the editor work, the library is saved once); one action at a time. The
  other commands that act on entries read the keys of `papers list -K` with
  -, e.g. `papers list smith -K | papers check -`

  --delete              remove the listed entries, as `papers rm` (asks
                        whether to delete their files, in a terminal)
  --delete-files        with --delete: also delete their files, as `papers rm
                        --delete-files` (an error in a shallow library)
  --keep-files          with --delete: keep their files, without asking
  -e, --edit            edit the listed entries in a text editor, as `papers
                        edit`
  --add-keywords, --add-tag ADD_KEYWORDS [ADD_KEYWORDS ...]
                        add keywords (tags) to the listed entries, as `papers
                        tag --add`
  --rename              place the files of the listed entries under their
                        template name, as `papers file rename`
  --keep-source         with --rename: keep the files where they are too, as
                        `papers file rename --keep-source`
  -o, --open            open the files of the listed entries, as `papers open`
  --attach FILE [FILE ...]
                        attach files to the listed entry, as `papers file
                        attach KEY FILE...` (the files setting applies); an
                        error unless the listing gives exactly one entry
  --rm-tag TAG [TAG ...]
                        remove tags from the listed entries, as `papers tag
                        --rm`
  --detach [FILE ...]   remove the links of the listed entries to these files
                        (without FILE: all their links), as `papers file
                        detach FILE... --key KEY...`
  --detach-broken       remove the broken links of the listed entries, as
                        `papers file detach --broken --key KEY...`
  --fix-files [DIR ...]
                        repair the file links of the listed entries, as
                        `papers file fix KEY...`; the broken links are also
                        looked for in the folders DIR, as `papers file fix
                        --search DIR`
  --move                move the files found in the --fix-files folders
                        instead of copying them (a file in the files directory
                        of another library is still copied); with --rename:
                        files mode move, whatever the setting
  --push                push the listed entries, as `papers push KEY...`
  --pull                pull the listed entries, as `papers pull KEY...`
  --sync                sync the listed entries, as `papers sync KEY...`
  --pool PATH           with --push, --pull, --sync: the library to exchange
                        with instead of the pool, as their --pool; with --fix-
                        files: also look for the files of the broken links in
                        the library PATH, as `papers file fix --pool PATH`
                        (can be repeated)
  --on-duplicate {ask,keep,update,skip,error}
                        what to do with an entry changed on both sides since
                        the last pull or push: ask (dialogue; the default in a
                        terminal), keep (the values of the side that receives
                        the changes are kept: the library's in a pull, the
                        pool's in a push), update (the values of the side they
                        come from are taken: the pool's in a pull, the
                        library's in a push), skip (the entry is left as it
                        is, and comes again next time), error (stop before
                        saving; the default without a terminal). Fields
                        changed on one side only need no decision.
  --export DIR          write the listed entries as a new library in DIR, as
                        `papers export DIR KEY...`
  --export-files {copy,link,none}
                        copy the files into DIR/files (a hard link when
                        possible; default), link to them where they are, or
                        leave the file links out
  --export-format FORMAT
                        the files of entries written in DIR: bib (papers.bib,
                        the default: DIR is a papers library), ris
                        (papers.ris), csl-json (papers.json), bibjson
                        (papers.bib.json), or all (RIS needs the rispy
                        package); repeat the option or separate the formats
                        with commas, e.g. --export-format bib,ris

place the files of the entries (all entries without KEY) in the files
directory, under the name made from the name template. The files already there

library (inside its files directory) is copied, not moved.

                        ids field works too); - reads them from the standard
                        input, one per line

                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
